With that land, Congress created ten new national parks. But in drawing the boundaries of those new parks, Congress made an unusual choice. Instead of enclosing only lands the Federal Government owns, Congress decided to track Alaska's natural terrain. The result was to sweep into the parks more than 18 million acres of land owned by the State, Native tribes, or private parties.
